shortDescription: Thailand's trade account was in balance in July, the Bank of Thailand said on Monday.

children: Thailand's trade account was in balance in July, the Bank of Thailand said on Monday.
Exports (THEXP=ECI) rose 22.3% in July from a year earlier, the central bank said.
Imports (THIMP=ECI) rose 35.5% and the current account showed a $1.6 billion deficit in July.
Private consumption rose 1.2% from a month earlier, while private investment dropped 0.3% from June.
The economy expanded in July from June, the central bank said, but added that its recovery would be uneven.
Last week, the central bank left its key interest rate unchanged at 1.00%, saying economic growth was low and uneven.
In June, the central bank forecast economic growth of 2.3% this year, close to last year's 2.4% growth. It forecast growth of 1.8% in 2027.
Southeast Asia's second-largest economy expanded 1.9% annually in the second quarter of 2026, down sharply from 2.8% in the previous quarter.
